h.strategy: Favor hypotheses driven by strong structural mechanisms: (1) an edit matters less when the part it modifies is disconnected, bypassed, or redundant in the parent; (2) diminishing returns: adding capacity helps less when the parent already has plenty, and removing it hurts more when the parent has little; (3) bottlenecks: improving a component helps more when it is the sole path or limiting factor. Prefer conditions that change the edit's effect by a large amount over subtle ones. Avoid hypotheses whose direction depends on fine balances between competing effects. State each hypothesis's mechanism in one sentence.

hyps.why: With edge 0 removed, node 1 carries no signal, so upgrading edge 4 modifies a dead path.
Edge 2 takes input from node 1, which is empty when edge 0 is none, so the edit has nothing to act on.
Node 2 reaches the output only through edge 5, so with edge 5 removed edge 1 is disconnected.
Edge 2 feeds node 2, which has no path to the output when edge 5 is none.
Replacing none reconnects node 2 to the output, a much larger gain than upgrading an existing op.
Replacing none reconnects node 2 to the output, a larger gain than swapping one existing op for another.
Edge 3 is always a live direct path, so filling an empty slot with a conv3x3 gains more than replacing an existing op.
Replacing none opens a whole new path, a larger gain than swapping one op for another.
Adding a skip where the direct edge was absent gives a large gain, while replacing any existing op gives much less.
Removing a conv3x3 loses the most capacity on the direct path, while removing a weaker op or a none costs less.
